newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE warns against delay in Albania force, polls.
newsitem.headline: OSCE warns against delay in Albania force, polls.

text.p: European mediator Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday a multinational force had to arrive in Albania as soon as possible to avoid a further flood of refugees from the lawless state.
Vranitzky, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's special envoy to Albania, also stressed it was crucial fresh elections were held on schedule before the end of June.

Speaking on his return from Athens where he met Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and Greek and Italian leaders, Vranitzky said any delay in deploying a multinational force would exacerbate the volatile situation in the Balkan state.
"If the time element isn't respected, then we'll see an escalation of the refugee crisis," the former Austrian chancellor told a news conference.
Albania has been swept by violence since January when a string of fraudulent investment schemes collapsed, wiping out the savings of thousands of people.

Rioting turned into rebellion across the country, with most insurgents pinning the blame for the pyramid scheme scandal on President Sali Berisha. Most of the south still remains outside government control.
Vranitzky said the OSCE proposed a two-pronged approach to protecting aid deliveries and establishing security.

The "step-by-step" approach would focus on establishing security in one key area such as the Adriatic port of Durres, from where forces would fan out to expand protection for aid deliveries across the country.
Another aim would be to secure the functioning of a transit route from neighbouring Macedonia in the northeast to Albania's southern regions to enable safe passage for relief convoys.

Fino, who heads Albania's all-party crisis government, won support in Athens from the European Union and the OSCE for organisational, economic and humanitarian aid as well as an Italian-led force to protect relief supplies.

So far, Italy is expected to provide between 2,000 and 2,500 troops, France 1,000, Greece 700, Turkey 500, Spain 500 and Romania 400. Austria and Bulgaria have also said they are prepared to contribute troops.
Italy said it expected to be able to start deploying the multi-national force of around 5,000 men around April 12.
Asked in Athens if the April 12 deadline was realistic, Vranitzky said: "Meeting this deadline is a bit over-optimistic but things won't change if we have plus or minus five days."
But he was insistent that a timetable for a fresh general election by the end of June should be respected to avoid the risk of indefinite postponement.
"Some in Albania see this date as too early -- that you can't have elections when people are still shooting at each other. But it's no good postponing it," he said in Vienna.

Albania's last general election last May was boycotted by most opposition parties which accused Berisha's Democratic Party of rigging the polls. Foreign observers also criticised the polls in which the Democrats won most seats in parliament.
